newsitem.title: FRANCE: Big "Yes" vote in Algeria referendum - state radio.
newsitem.headline: Big "Yes" vote in Algeria referendum - state radio.

text.p: Algerians have voted overwhelming in favour of a draft constitution that would ban Islamic political parties, Algeria's state radio reported on Friday.
The radio, basing its report on provisional referendum returns from several regions, said there would be a large "yes" vote.

State media said threats of violence by Moslem militants did not materialise. Official figures showed Algerians had turned out in large numbers to vote in defiance of the threats and calls by main opposition leaders for a boycott.
Polls closed at 8 p.m. (1900) on Thursday but by early evening nearly three-quarters of Algeria's 16.4 million eligible voters had cast ballots, state radio said, quoting the Interior Ministry.

Residents in the garrison town of Blida, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, said the army shelled mountains near the city on Wednesday night, apparently trying to pre-empt any buildup of Moslem guerrillas. Blida is a route for Moslem guerrillas seeking to carry out attacks around Algiers.
The constitution would ban Moslem militants from gaining power and guerrillas threatened before the referendum that they would kill anyone voting.
